subject: Private deployment: phased pinning window & canary evacuation plan
messages:
From: Paula Sanders <paula.sanders@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment patching — constraints and target windows

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for taking this. We’re planning the next maintenance cycle for our private Redwood deployment (VPC, single-region) and need to lock down a patch cadence that meets our compliance and clinical-availability constraints. High-level asks:

- Minimal disruption to our API (SLA: 99.95% during business hours)
- Strict version pinning for major model/runtime changes, but we want minor security patches applied quickly
- A safe, rehearsed rollback/evacuation method in case of regressions that affect inference correctness or KV cache integrity

Attached is our internal maintenance requirements matrix (ACME_maintenance_req.xlsx). Can you propose a phased window approach that includes a canary evacuation (swap to warm nodes) and an explicit escape hatch? Also flagged: our network team requires documentation for flows that touch our BGP edge and the firewall rules that Redwood’s orchestrator will briefly open for healthchecks.

Goal: pick a maintenance cadence we can agree on for Q4 and a rehearsal date in September.

Thanks,
Paula
Paula Sanders
Director, Platform Operations
Acme Health

[Attachment: ACME_maintenance_req.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Paula Sanders <paula.sanders@acmehealth.com>, ops@acmehealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — constraints and target windows

Paula — thanks, good context.

Quick summary (high level proposal):
1) Cadence: quarterly major pin windows + weekly minor-security micro-rolls. Major pins require a 2-week notice; micro-rolls can be scheduled with 48h notice.
2) Phased window (recommended template): preflight -> canary evacuation -> staggered node patch -> verification -> final cutover. Typical business-hours-safe window: 02:00–06:00 local with 20% canary traffic shift first.
3) Canary evacuation / swap: maintain a warm standby fleet (same model pin) in a separate subnet. During canary we shift 20% traffic for 30m, validate end-to-end traces + token-level latency/cost, then proceed.
4) Escape hatch: automated immediate rollback if any of the following triggers fire within the 60m post-patch: 15% increase in error rate, 25% regression on token-level probability drift for monitored prompts, or latency p95 increase > 2x.
5) Network considerations: healthcheck ports will be limited to Acme CIDR and a short-lived ephemeral port range; we’ll provide a firewall delta script and BGP guidance for route reflex during migration.

Attachments: proposed cadence and window matrix (redwood_proposed_patch_cadence.pdf). I’ve also attached a short preflight checklist we run for Dedicated/Private deployments.

If that aligns, Monica and Dev will sketch the detailed playbook (drain commands, cache invalidation order, KV-handoff strategy) and we can pick rehearsal dates.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding the engineering playbook details we’ll need for Acme’s network/security team. High level technical bullets below — I’ll push a full markdown playbook (drain-playbook.md) after internal review.

Preflight checklist (must clear before any window):
- Cluster health: all nodes Ready; no crashlooping pods; KV cache eviction under threshold
- Telemetry snapshot: baseline traces and token-prob arrays saved (30m window)
- DB / persistence snapshot: last successful backup verified, retention tag created
- Network: ephemeral healthcheck ACLs staged; firewall change approved in ticket.

Canary evacuation sequence (step-by-step):
1) Create canary slice (20% of pods) in warm subnet; replicate KV snapshot and warm caches.
2) Shift 20% of traffic with canary routing rule; hold 30 minutes.
3) Run automated evaluation suite: latency (p50/p95), error-rate, prompt-regression tests (we’ll use customer-specific prompt set).
4) If pass -> proceed to staggered drain/patch. If fail -> immediate rollback (see escape hatch below).

Staggered drain/patch order:
- Control-plane pods (replicas) -> inferencer nodes (drain one rack at a time) -> warm cache rehydrate -> Promote patched nodes back to rotation.
- Pause between racks: 10–15 minutes for system stabilization

KV cache integrity note: our preference is a cold-reload for major runtime changes. For minor patches that don’t touch cache format, we do an in-place restart with cache warmup. We’ll document a deterministic cache checkpoint/rehydration order to avoid split-brain.

Escape hatch / rollback triggers (engineer-level):
- Immediate: crashloops > 3 nodes in 10m, token-prob drift > 25% on monitored prompts, or sustained error-rate > 15% above baseline
- Controlled rollback: if we see performance regressions between 10–15% but non-failure, we trigger a staged rollback of the most recent rack and increase canary coverage to isolate fault.

Network-specific items:
- BGP: minimize route withdrawal; we will prefer traffic-weighting over hard route changes. If BGP flap risk is high, we’ll avoid route withdrawals and do application-level weights only.
- Firewall: healthcheck IPs will be ephemeral; provide an iptables/ACL diff for Acme to stage.

I’ll attach the playbook and the exact drain commands (kubectl drain flags, systemd restart sequence) in the follow up.

[Attachment: drain-playbook.md (text/markdown)]

Thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we commit to a rehearsal date:

- For major runtime pins that require cold cache rehydration, what typical downtime should we budget per rack? (We need a number for our incident runbook.)
- If we hit the immediate rollback trigger during a weekday business window, do you have an automated path to restore prior KV checkpoints, or is that manual today?

Also, please confirm whether the quarantine ACL changes and healthcheck ports will require any DNS TTL changes on our side. Our network team is nervous about fast DNS swaps during windows.

Paula

Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — constraints and target windows

Paula — short answers and next steps: 

1) Downtime per rack (major cold-rehydrate): budget 6–12 minutes per rack for rehydrate + validation. The variable depends on model size and cache warmup. We’ll provide a measured estimate after a rehearsal run against your snapshot (we expect 8m median for your current config).

2) KV recovery: we support an automated checkpoint restore path. In a rollback, our orchestrator can point nodes at the previous checkpoint and stream the KV index; full rehydrate may still take minutes, but the switch is automated (we’ve exercised this in two customer rehearsals this year). We’ll include the exact CLI steps in the final playbook.

3) DNS / ACLs: you should avoid short TTL flips mid-window. We’ll avoid DNS changes by using application-layer routing weight shifts and ephemeral ACLs restricted to your CIDR. The firewall delta we send is additive and short-lived — no DNS swap required.

Next steps: Monica will share the full drain-playbook.md and we’ll propose two rehearsal dates in September (2026-09-10 and 2026-09-17). If either of those work, please confirm and we’ll lock the 02:00–06:00 window for rehearsals. Once rehearsed, we’ll run quarterly major pins on a mutually agreed calendar and maintain weekly micro-rolls for security patches.

I’ll attach the signed schedule template once you confirm.

Best,
—Karthik
